deep.reconstruction:
This page is a handwritten table of contents for a projected EGA chapter on group schemes. The heading reads 'EGA Chap. VI – Schémas en groupes et torseurs'. An older title, probably 'fibrés principaux homogènes', is struck through and replaced by 'torseurs'. That matches the terminology shift of the mid-1960s (Giraud, SGA 4). Under the old 1960 plan in the EGA introduction, the group-scheme chapter was Ch. VII ('Schémas en groupes, espaces fibrés principaux'). The archive folder is titled 'Plan EGA VII', yet the page itself says 'Chap. VI'. So either the chapters were being renumbered, or this sheet belongs to a reorganised plan.

The plan has three parts.

(A) Propriétés générales
- §1: general techniques. The likely reading is 'passing from one point to all points' by homogeneity under translations: a property of a group scheme or homogeneous space that holds at one point (or over an open set) holds everywhere. Open properties of morphisms would be used together with general properties of morphisms from EGA IV.
- §2: neutral component G^0, dimension, separatedness. For example, a group locally of finite type over a field is separated; dim G equals the dimension at the identity.
- §3: affine groups.
- §4: subgroups generated by a family of morphisms. This is the content of SGA 3 VI_B §7.
- §5: passage to the quotient, i.e. homogeneous spaces and quotient groups.
- §6: probably 'G^τ et G^0', with a reference read here as TDTE VI no. 1. TDTE VI is Grothendieck's Bourbaki talk 'Le schéma de Picard: propriétés générales'. As I recall, it begins with generalities on group preschemes, which would cover G^0 and the subgroup G^τ of points with a multiple in G^0. That subgroup is what is needed to define Pic^τ.
- A marginal brace over §3–§5 carries an illegible note. It possibly restricts these sections to the case 'sur un corps'.

(B) Étude infinitésimale
- §7: infinitesimal extension problems. These include lifting of homomorphisms, sections and torsors, and the vanishing or obstruction groups in Hochschild cohomology. The reference given is SGA 3 (SGAD).
- §8: the hyperalgebra of a group, i.e. its distribution algebra in Dieudonné's and Cartier's sense; the Lie algebra; invariant differential operators.
- §9: probably 'problème inverse', i.e. recovering a (formal or infinitesimal) group from its hyperalgebra or Lie data.
- §10: radicial (infinitesimal) groups and p-Lie algebras. This is the equivalence between height-one radicial group schemes and restricted Lie algebras, as in SGA 3 VII_A and Demazure–Gabriel.
- §11: Cartier duality. A heading '(C) Dualité de Cartier' has been crossed out and absorbed as §11.

(C) Groupes de type multiplicatif
- Rigidity properties tied to points of finite order: density of torsion subgroups and rigidity of homomorphisms from multiplicative-type groups.
- 'Maximum : SGAD VIII, IX, X' means the most this part should contain is the material of SGA 3 Exposés VIII (diagonalisable groups), IX (groups of multiplicative type) and X (characterisation, classification and rigidity).
- §12 is left blank.

The plan is therefore a condensation into EGA of the SGA 3 foundations, explicitly stopping before reductive groups.

The faint typed text showing through belongs to the next sheet: a typed draft (no. 7.9) on representing fibre functors of a topos as pseudo-filtered inductive limits of representables, and on comparing them with pro-schemes. It is unrelated to this plan.
errors: No mathematical claims are made, only section titles, so there is nothing to be wrong.
The chapter number (VI) does not match the folder title 'Plan EGA VII' or the 1960 EGA plan, where group schemes are Ch. VII. This is probably a renumbering, not an error.

missed.claim: This is a historiographical detail of the never-written EGA group-scheme chapter. It is renumbered as Ch. VI, retitled from 'fibrés principaux' to 'torseurs', and its scope is explicitly capped at SGA 3 VIII–X, so reductive groups are excluded. It shows how Grothendieck intended to absorb SGA 3 into EGA. It is of minor interest for the history of the EGA plan, not a mathematical discovery.

deep.surprise_reason: A table of contents whose content all appears in SGA 3 and FGA. The only novelty is a small archival fact about chapter numbering and scope.
transcription_corrections: §1 probably reads 'passage d'un point à tout' (homogeneity under translation) rather than 'd'un k'. The first word is uncertain ('Utilisation'?), not clearly 'Histoire'.
§6 likely reads 'G^τ et G^0 (cf TDTE VI n° 1)'. 'FDTE' is probably 'TDTE' (Techniques de descente et théorèmes d'existence, FGA).
The §7 reference may be 'SGAD III' (SGA 3 Exp. III, Extensions infinitésimales) rather than 'SGAD II'; the numeral is ambiguous in the image.
§10: the struck word is 'Alg.'; the line reads 'Groupes radiciels et p-algèbres de Lie'. The word 'Lie' is added above the line.
Section (C) reads 'Groupes de type mult. ; propriétés de rigidité liées aux pts d'ordre fini'.
The faint typed text in the background is bleed-through from the typed draft on fibre functors (cf. next page); it is not part of this page's content.
